QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_14

question.text: For a listed company buyback occurring on or after October 1, 2024, which of the following correctly describes the tax treatment per the current NISM X-B workbook?

answer.text: The company pays buyback tax under Section 115QA and the shareholder's receipt is exempt under Section 10(34A)

The buyback proceeds are taxed in the hands of the shareholder as dividend (Income from Other Sources); the shareholder's cost of acquisition is treated as a capital loss eligible for setoff/carry-forward; there is no buyback tax in the hands of the company
Both the company and shareholder are taxed — company on distributed income and shareholder on capital gains
The buyback is completely tax-free for both the company and the shareholder

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current NISM X-B workbook (post-Budget 2024), for buybacks on or after October 1, 2024, proceeds received by shareholders are taxed as dividend (Income from Other Sources); the cost of the bought-back shares is treated as a capital loss available for setoff and carry-forward as per capital-gains rules. The earlier company-level buyback tax under Section 115QA and shareholder exemption under Section 10(34A) do not apply for buybacks after that date. The Trap: Option A applies the legacy Section 115QA / Section 10(34A) regime, which is no longer in force for post-October-1, 2024 buybacks. Option C creates double taxation; Option D ignores the dividend treatment. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-B tests the shift from company-level buyback tax to shareholder-level dividend taxation; Merchant Banking (Series IX) tests the corporate-action mechanics of buybacks.
